scope: Two bounded source-bound original Doom E1M1 timing windows beginning at pre-increment leveltime tic 70; sanitized counters only.
interpretation: The Doom leveltime delta difference reverses sign relative to the prior 1800 ms start-tic-70 observation (DOSBox-X +59 versus QEMU +63, difference -4): at 300 ms the difference is +2 and at 900 ms it is +5. This is a window-dependent sign reversal across the recorded lengths, not evidence of a stable fixed offset or timing rate.
uncertainty: DOSBox-X threshold detection polls then pauses; endpoints are non-atomic and observed PIC elapsed time includes polling/pause latency.
DOSBox-X PIC guest milliseconds and QEMU virtual nanoseconds are separate clock domains; no common-clock comparison is claimed.
BDA endpoints have independent, uncalibrated phases; matching tick deltas do not establish calibrated elapsed-time equivalence.
Input history and prepared states remain bounded to these runs; no audio was captured.
Two window lengths and the prior 1800 ms observation do not establish general timing parity, failure, fixed offset, or rate.
private_artifact_exclusion: Raw receipts and two DOSBox endpoint JSON files are preserved in the private evidence area. No game media, FDB, VM state, screenshots or audio are included here.
